cards.text: Ezekiel is a priest living among the exiles, far from home (Ezekiel 1:1-3). In the sixth year, he's sitting in his house with the elders of Judah sitting before him. And right there, in the middle of company, the hand of the Lord GOD falls on him.

cards.question: Ezekiel looks and sees a figure like that of a man. From His waist up, He's as bright as the gleam of amber. From His waist down, what does His appearance look like?

cards.text: He stretches out what looked like a hand and takes Ezekiel by the hair of his head. The HAIR, friend, and with a mustache this size, I felt that one all the way down to my gold base.

cards.question: Then the Spirit lifts Ezekiel up between earth and heaven and carries him in visions of God to ___.
Ezekiel ends up at the entrance of the north gate of the inner court. What's seated right there?

answers.text: A golden statue of the king
The high priest of the temple

cards.text: And there Ezekiel sees the glory of the God of Israel, like the vision he saw in the plain. God tells him to lift his eyes to the north, and there it is again, that idol of jealousy, at the entrance north of the Altar Gate.

cards.question: God asks Ezekiel if he sees what the house of Israel is doing. God says these great abominations are driving Him far from His sanctuary.
God isn't finished showing Ezekiel around. What does He say Ezekiel will still see?

cards.text: Next, God brings Ezekiel to the entrance to the court, and Ezekiel spots a hole in the wall. Friend, I lived in the back of a junk drawer for years, and I can tell you: nothing back there ever wanted to be found.

cards.question: At the hole in the wall, God tells Ezekiel to leave the wall alone and just peek through the hole.

cards.text: So Ezekiel digs through the wall and finds a doorway. You know when you pull the couch out to vacuum and find things that make you question your whole life? Yeah. This is WORSE.

God tells him to go in and see the wicked abominations they're committing there. Ezekiel looks, and engraved all around the wall is every kind of crawling creature and detestable beast, along with all the idols of the house of Israel.

cards.question: Inside that hidden room, who's standing in front of all those engravings?

cards.text: Jaazaniah son of Shaphan stands among them, and each man has a censer in his hand, with a fragrant cloud of incense rising. Seventy grown men in a secret room behind a wall, and they made sure it SMELLS nice.

cards.question: The elders are doing this in the darkness, each at the shrine of his own idol. They're saying the LORD does not see them.

cards.text: They also say the LORD has forsaken the land. Meanwhile, God is right there, giving Ezekiel a guided tour of the room. He sees you, fellas. He sees you.

Again, God tells Ezekiel he'll see them committing even greater abominations, and friend, this tour has more levels than a parking garage. Then He brings Ezekiel to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD.

cards.question: At the north gate of the house of the LORD, Ezekiel sees ___ sitting there, weeping for Tammuz.

cards.text: God asks him, "do you see this?" and says there are even greater abominations than these. Then He brings Ezekiel into the inner court, to the entrance to the temple of the LORD, between the portico and the altar.

cards.question: About twenty-five men are standing between the portico and the altar. They're facing the temple of the LORD.
With their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east, what are these twenty-five men bowing to in worship?

cards.text: Backs to the house of the LORD, bowing to the sun. That's like turning your back on your boss on payday... so you can go thank the ATM.
God asks Ezekiel, "do you see this?" Then He asks if the abominations they're practicing here aren't enough for the house of Judah.

cards.question: God says the house of Judah must also fill the land with ___ and continually provoke Him to anger.

cards.text: And then one more: "Look, they are even putting the branch to their nose!"

cards.question: After everything God has shown Ezekiel, how does God say He will respond?
God says that if they shout loudly in His ears, He will listen to them.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Ezekiel has seen a LOT, and trust me, this vision isn't finished.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess a descriptive detail of the vision (fire vs polished bronze vs flowing water). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason it out. This matches the Psalm 23 bad example of guessing a detail such as oil, myrrh or perfume.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: The answers are not the same kind of thing. Two are objects (an idol and a statue) and one is a person (the high priest). The right answer also sounds more like the Bible than the others.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question's setup line, 'God isn't finished showing Ezekiel around,' rules out the wrong answer 'Nothing worse than this.' The wrong answer 'The people tearing it down' is also vague: it doesn't say what 'it' is, and it isn't the same kind of thing as the right answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke says nothing in the junk drawer ever wanted to be found. That contradicts his backstory, where everyone in the drawer held their breath hoping someone would remember them and put them back to work. The comparison also doesn't click: a hidden idol room isn't like forgotten drawer items.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of God's speech ('fill the land with ___'). The earlier cards give nothing that lets the baker reason their way to violence over lies or famine.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The line saying the story isn't over nearly copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.') instead of being an original line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Tammuz appears for the first time with no word about who he is. The passage itself doesn't identify him.
findings.question: Does the 'New people' rule (say simply who they are) apply to a deity like Tammuz, even though identifying him needs an outside source? Or is a name like this left to the dictionary pop-up, under 'Don't spend card words explaining a hard word'?
